citation: "Residence of John Kinzie." — lithograph by Napoleon Sarony from a sketch by Mrs. John H. Kinzie, reproduced as a plate in J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912), ch. II.
author: Napoleon Sarony, lithographer, after a sketch by Juliette A. (Mrs. John H.) Kinzie
date: 1912 (the reproduction); Sarony's lithograph is of the 1850s
describes_date: the house as the Kinzies had it, which Currey's caption puts at 1804-1813 and 1816-1828
repository: Project Gutenberg eBook #52346 (images/residence_john_kinzie.png); the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_kinzie_residence_sarony_currey_1912.png (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md)
locator: the plate captioned 'RESIDENCE OF JOHN KINZIE.' in ch. II, 656 x 391 px as Project Gutenberg serves it
rights_note: Published 1912 in the United States, out of copyright by age; Sarony's lithograph is older still.
access_notes: Fetched from Project Gutenberg and read off the image itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2498). The caption is quoted from the Gutenberg text: 'The house in which John Kinzie and his family lived from 1804 to 1813, and again from 1816 to 1828, as it was lithographed by Sarony from a sketch made by Mrs. John H. Kinzie, the author of Wau-Bun.'
what_it_supplies: the house long and low under a gable roof along the river, the east end toward the eye's right, a piazza across the front on posts with a rail
a picket fence round the green before the house down toward the water, a landing at the water's edge
four columnar Lombardy poplars in a row east of the house running toward the river, and a great broad-crowned tree behind it
two stacks through the ridge, and outbuildings and a two-storey house up the road to the west, behind the house
what_it_does_not_supply: the house in 1812 as distinct from the 1820s: the caption covers both
note: The one picture of the house drawn by a member of the household: Juliette Kinzie lived beside it from 1831. The Teich postcard's painting and Kirkland's 1893 plate are the same composition. No camera is solved for it yet (T-2516).
